log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Skarmory

decisions.rationale: Lead Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl (proven Game 1 anti-sun core: Fake Out disruption, screens, Rock Slide SE on both Fire-types). Back Gholdengo (immune to Aegislash Sacred Sword, resists Venusaur SolarBeam/Sludge Bomb, walls Heracross, Shadow Ball SE on Aegislash) and Tauros (Intimidate, Wave Crash for Torkoal, Aqua Jet priority, Close Combat for Skarmory). Drop Excadrill since Torkoal Drought overwrites sand on entry making Sand Rush unreliable; drop Gengar since Gholdengo covers the Aegislash/Heracross matchups more durably while Tauros provides the Intimidate/priority Gengar lacks.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 bring: Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl+Gholdengo+Tauros. Dropped Excadrill (Torkoal Drought overwrites sand on simultaneous entry — slower weather ability wins, so Sand Rush unreliable vs sun core) and Gengar (Gholdengo covers Aegislash/Heracross more durably). Gholdengo key: immune to Sacred Sword (Fighting vs Steel/Ghost=0), resists Venusaur SolarBeam/Sludge Bomb (0.5x each), walls Heracross (CC immune, Megahorn NVE), Shadow Ball SE on Aegislash. Grimmsnarl resists Heracross STABs, Spirit Break SE on Heracross. Tauros Close Combat immune on Aegislash (Fighting vs Ghost=0) but SE on Skarmory. If opponent leads Venusaur+Charizard-Y: keep Tyranitar alive to re-establish sand on re-entry (overwrites sun since Torkoal Drought only triggers on initial entry), suppress Chlorophyll. Grimmsnarl Light Screen priority vs special-heavy sun team. Opponent may counter-lead expecting Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl from Game 1 — Heracross lead threatens 4x CC on Tyranitar but Grimmsnarl handles it.

decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard and Torkoal to establish immediate offensive pressure and sun support; Charizard's 161 SpA with Solar Power in sun makes it the primary special win-condition, while Torkoal's Drought + Heat Rock lock sun to power FireBlast and enable Venusaur's free SolarBeam. Back picks Venusaur (Chlorophyll speed in sun, free SolarBeam, SE coverage on Gengar/Gholdengo) and Skarmory (Sturdy physical wall to absorb Excadrill/Tyranitar/Tauros hits, Spikes pressure, Whirlwind phazing). This lineup prioritizes special offense to bypass opponent's Light Screen + sand combination while Skarmory handles their physical sweepers.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Sand Stream offense core: Tyranitar Adamant Smooth Rock, Excadrill Jolly Life Orb Sand Rush. Grimmsnarl Light Clay Prankster dual screens. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua Adamant Intimidate physical breaker. Gengar (Timid Gengarite) and Gholdengo (Modest Leftovers) are unbrought special reserves. CharizarditeY expended this series. Opponent 4th slot confirmed Tauros. Screens + sand require sustained special pressure to break; preserve physical attackers for later. Sun team synergizes with Charizard Solar Power, Venusaur Chlorophyll, and Torkoal Drought.

decisions.rationale: Charizard Focus Blast is a guaranteed OHKO on Tyranitar (142-207%) and Charizard outspeeds both my Pokémon. Fake Out (priority +3) flinches Charizard before it can act, then Tyranitar's Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO back (104-196%, 4x Rock vs Fire/Flying). If Charizard Protects to bait Fake Out, Rock Slide still chunks Torkoal for 37-63%, and Torkoal's worst hit on Tyranitar (Solar Beam) only does 39-60% — Tyranitar survives in every branch. Light Screen can't guarantee survival (Focus Blast still 71-104% through screen), so Fake Out is the only reliable way to protect Tyranitar turn 1 while simultaneously removing the deadliest threat.
decisions.notebook: Sun team key damage benchmarks: Charizard Focus Blast = guaranteed OHKO on Tyranitar (4x, 142-207%); Charizard Solar Beam = possible OHKO (71-104%); Torkoal Solar Beam = 39-60% on Tyranitar (survivable); Torkoal Eruption = only 20-31% on Tyranitar. Tyranitar Rock Slide = guaranteed OHKO on Charizard (4x, 104-196%) and 37-63% on Torkoal. Fake Out on Charizard is mandatory to prevent Focus Blast KO since Charizard outspeeds Tyranitar. Solar Power chips Charizard 12.5%/turn in sun. Plan: eliminate Charizard ASAP, then Light Screen to neuter remaining special attackers (Torkoal/Venusaur). Keep Tyranitar alive to re-establish Sand on re-entry (overwrites sun if Torkoal already fainted). Gholdengo in back walls Aegislash/Heracross; Tauros handles Skarmory.

decisions.rationale: Charizard Focus Blast targets Tyranitar for a guaranteed OHKO without screens (4x SE, 139-247%) and massive damage even through LightScreen (69-123%). This is the highest-damage option available since CharizarditeY is expended and Mega Evolution is unavailable. Torkoal uses Eruption (spread, 150 BP Fire) which gets a 1.5x sun boost to 225 effective BP, dealing heavy neutral damage to Grimmsnarl after Tyranitar faints. Grimmsnarl will likely act first via Prankster to set a screen, but Focus Blast's 4x multiplier still produces extreme damage through it.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Sand Stream offense core: Tyranitar Adamant Smooth Rock, Excadrill Jolly Life Orb Sand Rush. Grimmsnarl Light Clay Prankster dual screens. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua Adamant Intimidate physical breaker. Gengar (Timid Gengarite) and Gholdengo (Modest Leftovers) are unbrought special reserves. CharizarditeY expended this series — no Mega available. Screens + sand require sustained special pressure to break; preserve physical attackers for later. Sun team synergizes with Charizard Solar Power, Venusaur Chlorophyll, and Torkoal Drought.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur with Chlorophyll in Sun outspeeds both active foes and threatens Tyranitar with super-effective Solar Beam and Grimmsnarl with Sludge Bomb, applying immediate special pressure while preserving physical attackers. Torkoal passes to regain momentum next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Sand Stream offense core: Tyranitar Adamant Smooth Rock, Excadrill Jolly Life Orb Sand Rush. Grimmsnarl Light Clay Prankster dual screens. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua Adamant Intimidate physical breaker. Gengar and Gholdengo are unbrought special reserves. CharizarditeY expended this series. Sun team synergizes with Chlorophyll Venusaur and Drought Torkoal. Prioritize special offense to break screens + sand; keep Skarmory and Torkoal as physical pivots for later.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Tyranitar)
decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl Light Screen via Prankster priority goes up before Venusaur moves, halving its SolarBeam (85.9-127.7% → ~43-64%) and SludgeBomb (68.6-102.1% → ~34-51%) to survivable ranges — without it either Pokémon can be OHKO'd. Tyranitar Thunder Wave on Venusaur (90% acc) permanently neuters Chlorophyll speed (220-290 → 55-72), making Venusaur slower than both my Pokémon next turn. Rock Slide on Torkoal is only a possible KO at 49% (37-63%) and doesn't address the Venusaur speed threat. Even if both foes SolarBeam Tyranitar through Light Screen (~62-94% combined), it survives. Paralyzing Venusaur is the highest-EV play for winning the speed race long-term.
decisions.notebook: Venusaur SolarBeam = 85.9-127.7% on Tyranitar (possible OHKO); SludgeBomb = 68.6-102.1% on Grimmsnarl (possible OHKO). Light Screen halves both to survivable. Torkoal SolarBeam = 38.7-59.7% on Tyranitar. Torkoal Eruption at 49% HP = only 9.4-15.2% on Tyranitar (negligible). Rock Slide on Torkoal = 37-63% (possible KO at 49%, not guaranteed). Plan: Light Screen + Thunder Wave Venusaur turn 2, then Rock Slide to clean Torkoal and chip paralyzed Venusaur turn 3. Keep Tyranitar alive to re-establish Sand when sun expires. Gholdengo in back walls Aegislash/Heracross; Tauros handles Skarmory. Opponent's 4th slot is one of Heracross/Skarmory/Aegislash.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur Solar Beam on Tyranitar exploits 2x STAB + 2x SE in sun (no charge turn) to eliminate the Sand Stream setter and biggest physical threat. Torkoal Eruption spreads damage to both foes, chipping Grimmsnarl while adding pressure on Tyranitar. This maximizes special offense to break through potential Light Clay screens and remove the sand core early.

Tyranitar at 10% is dead to any SE special hit from Venusaur or Torkoal. Switching to Gholdengo exploits its typing: Grass resisted by Steel (0.5x), Poison immune, and Sleep Powder blocked by Good as Gold. Solar Beam aimed at Tyranitar's slot hits Gholdengo for only 17-26% with Light Screen. Grimmsnarl Spirit Breaks Venusaur to drop its SpA one stage, neutering future Solar Beam/Sludge Bomb output. This preserves Tyranitar in back for a Sand Stream reset when sun expires (6 turns) and establishes Gholdengo as a Venusaur wall. Worst case (Sludge Bomb on Grimmsnarl, 45-68%) still leaves it alive at 17-40%.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 plan: Gholdengo walls Venusaur (resists Solar Beam 0.5x, immune Sludge Bomb + Sleep Powder via Good as Gold). Spirit Break SpA drops stack on Venusaur to reduce threat. Tyranitar preserved at 10% in back for Sand Stream reset when sun expires — switch it in to override Torkoal's Drought sun. Tauros in back for Torkoal (Wave Crash/Close Combat SE) and Skarmory (Close Combat SE). Gholdengo also handles Aegislash mirror with Shadow Ball SE. Watch for Heracross Close Combat (SE on Gholdengo's Steel typing) if it's the 4th. Series score 1-0; no need to overextend.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur Solar Beam into Tyranitar is a guaranteed KO (56-101% estimated damage on 10% HP through Light Screen). Torkoal Eruption spread applies chip damage to Grimmsnarl (11-22%) while the spread mechanic covers both foe slots. Removing Tyranitar now strips the opponent of their lead attacker and Sand Stream, degrading their defensive synergy with Light Screen.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Sand Stream offense core: Tyranitar Adamant Smooth Rock, Excadrill Jolly Life Orb Sand Rush. Grimmsnarl Light Clay Prankster dual screens. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua Adamant Intimidate physical breaker. Gengar and Gholdengo are unbrought special reserves. Sun team synergizes with Chlorophyll Venusaur and Drought Torkoal. Prioritize special offense to break screens + sand; keep Skarmory and Torkoal as physical pivots for later. CharizarditeY expended this series.

decisions.rationale: Gholdengo Recover heals to ~99% before Torkoal can Eruption (Speed 110 > 40-72), removing the KO threat from 49%. Grimmsnarl Spirit Break on Torkoal (Speed 90 > 40-72) drops its SpA by 1 before Eruption resolves, cutting future Eruption damage by ~33% and bringing Torkoal to ~34-40% HP for a Shadow Ball KO next turn. Even worst-case (Torkoal Protects or Grimmsnarl sleeps to Sleep Powder) leaves Gholdengo healthy and safe. Series lead 1-0, no need to overextend with risky offensive plays.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 plan intact: Gholdengo walls Venusaur (resists Solar Beam, immune Sludge Bomb/Sleep Powder via Good as Gold + Steel typing). Spirit Break SpA drops on Torkoal are priority to weaken Eruption. Tyranitar at 10% preserved for Sand Stream reset when needed — switch in to override sun, removing Chlorophyll and sun-boosted Eruption. Tauros in back for Torkoal (Wave Crash SE) and Skarmory (Close Combat SE). Shadow Ball on Torkoal at ~34-40% HP next turn should KO (39-76.6% range). Watch for Heracross as potential 4th (Close Combat SE on Gholdengo). Series score 1-0; prioritize preservation.

decisions.rationale: Sleep Powder on Grimmsnarl removes the opponent's screen setter and physical attacker, while Torkoal's Eruption spread in Sun with Drought exploits Gholdengo's Steel weakness for maximum damage on the most dangerous remaining threat.

Switch Grimmsnarl to Tyranitar to trigger Sand Stream, overriding sun — this strips Venusaur's Chlorophyll (speed drops to 55-72.5, below Gholdengo's 110) and makes Solar Beam two-turn again, while removing Torkoal's sun-boosted Eruption. Simultaneously, Gholdengo Shadow Ball KOs Torkoal (guaranteed: 39-76.6% vs 37% HP). Tyranitar at 10% likely survives incoming hits (Eruption NVE 3-5%, Sludge Bomb NVE 7-11% vs 10% HP — not a guaranteed KO). Even if Tyranitar falls, sand is permanently up and Tauros enters at 100% to clean up. If Torkoal Protects, it's stranded in sand with a neutered Eruption and Gholdengo KOs next turn while outspeeding everything.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 turn 5: Switched Grimmsnarl→Tyranitar for Sand Stream sun override + Gholdengo Shadow Ball on Torkoal (guaranteed KO at 37%). Key damage benchmarks: Shadow Ball Torkoal 39-76.6% (KO); Eruption on Gholdengo 16.3-27% (survives); Sludge Bomb on Tyranitar 7.3-11% vs 10% HP (not guaranteed KO); Eruption on Tyranitar 3.1-4.7% (survives). After sand: Venusaur speed 55-72.5 (no Chlorophyll), Gholdengo 110 outspeeds all. Solar Beam becomes two-turn without sun. Tauros in back at 100% for cleanup — Wave Crash SE on Torkoal, Close Combat SE on Skarmory. Watch Heracross Vacuum Wave (priority SE on Tauros/Tyranitar, but Gholdengo immune as Ghost). Series 1-0, prioritize preservation.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur Sludge Bomb into Grimmsnarl (2x SE, possible KO on the screens setter at 61% HP) is the highest-impact move—removing Grimmsnarl eliminates the Light Clay screens setter, Spirit Break, and Prankster status threat. Torkoal Eruption spread hits both foes, dealing super-effective damage to Gholdengo (Fire 2x into Steel/Ghost) for meaningful chip while pressuring the entire opposing side before Sandstorm can be set up.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Tyranitar at 4% is dead weight — switch to Tauros (100%, Intimidate, 138 Spe, Close Combat for Skarmory). Gholdengo Make It Rain has the highest KO odds on Venusaur at 47% (35.8-65.8% damage, ~60% KO chance vs Shadow Ball's ~45%). If Venusaur falls, it's Gholdengo+Tauros vs Skarmory alone — near-guaranteed win. SpA drop from Make It Rain is acceptable since Tauros handles Skarmory with Close Combat (27-59%) and Gholdengo can still Shadow Ball Skarmory (44-86%) for a 2HKO. Even if Venusaur survives or Protects, it's at very low HP and dies to sandstorm chip + Tauros Aqua Jet priority next turn. Venusaur's Sludge Bomb is immune on Gholdengo (Steel) and Sleep Powder fails (Good as Gold), so the main risk is Solar Beam charge — but Gholdengo resists Grass (0.5x) and Tauros can Protect next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Tauros Close Combat does 27-59% to Skarmory (neutral, Sturdy prevents OHKO). Gholdengo Shadow Ball does 44-86% to Skarmory — combined with Close Combat, can 2HKO. Make It Rain on Venusaur 36-66% (possible KO at 47%). Venusaur Sludge Bomb immune on Gholdengo, Sleep Powder blocked by Good as Gold. Solar Beam is 2-turn without sun (sand active). Tauros outspeeds all foe mons at 138. Series 1-0, prioritize closing out game 2. If game 3 needed, opponent has Heracross (Vacuum Wave priority SE on Tauros/Tyranitar, Gholdengo immune as Ghost) and Aegislash (FocusSash, StanceChange) available.

decisions.rationale: Sleep Powder on Tyranitar (7) disables the already-critical 3% Tyranitar, removing Thunder Wave and Earthquake threats entirely even if the opponent keeps it in. Spikes (0) from Skarmory sets up entry hazards for the unrevealed 4th Pokémon's inevitable switch-in. Gholdengo's likely Make It Rain will hit Venusaur for neutral Steel damage reduced by Light Screen (~0.5x), which Venusaur at 47% survives. Skarmory takes only 0.25x from its Steel resistance plus Light Screen. This turn maximizes long-term board pressure while the Sandstorm timer and Spikes wear down the opponent's remaining team.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Sand Stream core: Tyranitar Smooth Rock, Excadrill Life Orb Sand Rush, Grimmsnarl Light Clay dual screens. One unknown of Excadrill/Gengar/Tauros is the 4th. Sun synergizes with Chlorophyll Venusaur and Drought Torkoal. Prioritize special offense to break screens and sand; Skarmory and Torkoal are physical pivots. CharizarditeY expended this series. Gholdengo immune to Sleep Powder via Good as Gold.

decisions.rationale: Opponent has only Skarmory left (1v2). Skarmory has no attacking moves (Spikes/Whirlwind/Roost/Protect), so zero risk to both attacking. Tauros Close Combat (33.7-58.6%) + Gholdengo Shadow Ball (22.7-43.6% at SpA-2) = 56.4-102.2% combined, likely KOing Skarmory (72% HP). Whirlwind goes last (pri -6) so if we KO it never resolves. If Skarmory Protects, we simply retry next turn from an even more dominant position. Close Combat preferred over Wave Crash (same damage, no recoil, defense drops irrelevant vs a status-only Skarmory). Shadow Ball over Make It Rain (neutral vs NVE 0.5x, no further SpA drop).
decisions.notebook: Game 2 near-closing: opponent down to last mon Skarmory (no attacking moves). Gholdengo Shadow Ball at SpA-2 does 22.7-43.6% to Skarmory; Tauros Close Combat does 33.7-58.6%. Combined can KO from 72%. If game 3 needed: opponent brings Heracross (Jolly, Expert Belt, Moxie, Vacuum Wave priority SE on Tauros/Tyranitar, Gholdengo immune) and Aegislash (Careful, Focus Sash, StanceChange, King's Shield). Plan for game 3: lead Tauros+Gholdengo or Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl; watch for Heracross Vacuum Wave picking off weakened Tauros/Tyranitar; Gholdengo walls Aegislash Shadow Ball and Heracross Megahorn (Steel/Ghost resists Bug). Keep Gholdengo healthy as endgame cleaner.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur is fainted and can only pass. Skarmory uses Protect (+4 priority) to scout Tauros's move choice (WaveCrash vs AquaJet) and avoid all damage this turn while staying healthy behind Sandstorm immunity, preserving the only remaining Pokémon to gather intel for subsequent turns.

Skarmory is the opponent's last Pokémon at 77% with no attacking moves—only Spikes, Whirlwind, Roost, and Protect (reduced success rate after last-turn use). Shadow Ball (22.7–43.6%) + Close Combat (33.7–58.6%) = 56.4–102.2% combined, a strong chance to KO from 77%. Sturdy doesn't activate below 100% HP. Close Combat over Wave Crash avoids recoil since the Def/SpDef drops are irrelevant with no incoming attacks. If Skarmory Protects and it succeeds, we simply repeat next turn with Skarmory still unable to damage us. No risk either way.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 closing: opponent down to solo Skarmory (no attacking moves, only Spikes/Whirlwind/Roost/Protect). If game 3 needed: opponent brings Heracross (Jolly, Expert Belt, Moxie, Vacuum Wave priority SE on Tauros/Tyranitar, Gholdengo immune) and Aegislash (Careful, Focus Sash, StanceChange, King's Shield). Plan for game 3: lead Tauros+Gholdengo or Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl; watch for Heracross Vacuum Wave picking off weakened Tauros/Tyranitar; Gholdengo walls Aegislash Shadow Ball and Heracross Megahorn (Steel/Ghost resists Bug). Keep Gholdengo healthy as endgame cleaner. Skarmory Close Combat and Wave Crash deal identical 33.7–58.6%; prefer Close Combat to avoid Wave Crash recoil when no return damage threatens.

decisions.rationale: Skarmory is at 18% with no attacking moves—only Spikes/Whirlwind/Roost/Protect. Both Gholdengo Shadow Ball (22.7–43.6%) and Tauros Close Combat (26.7–58.6%) are guaranteed KOs from 18%. Sending in Tauros (89% HP, faster at 138 vs 90–122) gives the strongest offensive closer. Even if Skarmory Protects this coming turn, it can't Protect twice in a row, and Roost healing to ~68% still falls to combined damage next turn. Gholdengo stays active (Pass) to attack alongside Tauros next turn for the guaranteed KO and the 2-0 series win.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 closing: Skarmory solo at 18% with no attacking moves. Both Gholdengo Shadow Ball and Tauros Close Combat guaranteed KO from 18%. Send Tauros in for Tyranitar; double-attack next turn for the win. If Game 3 needed: opponent brings Heracross (Jolly Expert Belt Moxie, Vacuum Wave priority SE on Tauros/Tyranitar, Gholdengo immune) and Aegislash (Careful Focus Sash StanceChange King's Shield). Lead Tauros+Gholdengo or Tyranitar+Grimmsnarl; keep Gholdengo healthy as endgame cleaner; it walls Aegislash Shadow Ball and resists Heracross Megahorn. Watch for Heracross Vacuum Wave picking off weakened Tauros/Tyranitar. Skarmory Close Combat and Wave Crash both 33.7–58.6%; prefer Close Combat to avoid Wave Crash recoil when no return damage threatens.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur is fainted with no non-fainted teammates to switch in, so must pass. Skarmory should use Whirlwind on Tauros-Paldea-Aqua to force it out; the only available switch-in for the opponent is Tyranitar at 3% HP, which will die to Sandstorm. This leaves Skarmory facing only Gholdengo with Special Attack at -2, whose Make It Rain is doubly weakened (reduced SpA plus Skarmory's Steel resistance), making it easy to stall out and win.

Both Gholdengo Shadow Ball and Tauros Close Combat are guaranteed KOs on Skarmory at 18% HP. Sturdy won't save it below full HP. Double-targeting Skarmory guarantees the win this turn; if it Protects, both moves are harmlessly blocked and I repeat next turn. Skarmory has no offensive threat to punish the aggression.

Venusaur is fainted and can only pass. Skarmory at 19% HP needs immediate recovery; Roost heals to ~69%, making it far harder for the opponent's resisted Close Combat or neutral AquaJet to finish it off, keeping Skarmory alive as a pivot and hazard setter while the sandstorm and Light Screen timer work in my favor.

reflections.summary: Game 2 was a dominant 9-turn win secured by an excellent lead matchup and clean execution. Tyranitar's Sand Stream overrode the opponent's sun, and the Turn 1 Fake Out + Rock Slide combo eliminated Mega Charizard Y before it could act, instantly gutting the sun core. Thunder Wave on Venusaur paid off with a full paralysis on Turn 4, giving Gholdengo a free Recover. From there, Gholdengo and Tauros cleaned up Torkoal, Venusaur, and Skarmory without further losses. Zero decision errors. The series was won 2-0 because the registered roster hard-counters sun archetypes—Sand Stream disrupts Drought/Chlorophyll, Rock Slide hits the Fire/Grass core super effectively, and Gholdengo walls the residual special attackers.
reflections.adjustment: The Game 2 bring (Tyranitar, Grimmsnarl, Gholdengo, Tauros) was near-optimal against this sun squad and needs no changes if the opponent repeats the same four. If they adapt by bringing Heracross or Aegislash in a future rematch, keep Gholdengo healthy as the endgame cleaner—it resists Heracross's Megahorn and is immune to Aegislash's Shadow Ball. Consider leading Tauros + Gholdengo to threaten both Heracross (Intimidate + Close Combat) and Aegislash (Make It Rain) while preserving Tyranitar for sand control. Mega Gengar was unnecessary here but could trap Aegislash or Skarmory in a Game 3 scenario; weigh it if the opponent shifts toward bulkier structures.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors sun: Mega Charizard Y + Torkoal + Chlorophyll Venusaur core, with Skarmory for hazard/phasing support. Bench options are Heracross (Jolly Expert Belt Moxie; CloseCombat/Megahorn/RockBlast/VacuumWave) and Aegislash (Careful Focus Sash; King's Shield/Shadow Ball/SacredSword/SwordsDance). Opponent leads aggressively with both weather setters expecting to overwhelm; vulnerable to Fake Out + spread Rock Slide. Sand Stream Tyranitar is the cornerstone counter—always bring it. Venusaur is the main speed threat under sun; Thunder Wave or a fast KO neutralizes it. Skarmory uses Spikes + Whirlwind to disrupt positioning; Tauros Close Combat handles it cleanly. Opponent does not protect against sand chip on their Fire-types. If they adapt, expect Heracross as a speed/priority threat and Aegislash as a bulky setup pivot; Gholdengo is the primary answer to both. Mega Gengar remains untested this series but offers trapping utility against Skarmory or Aegislash if needed.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2. Game 2 was lost because the sun offense core collapsed before it could function. Charizard (Mega Stone holder) was flinch-locked by Grimmsnarl's Fake Out and OHKO'd by Tyranitar's Rock Slide on Turn 1, eliminating the sun synergy anchor and the Mega evolution investment before either contributed. The weather war was decisively lost: Tyranitar's Sand Stream overwrote Torkoal's Drought every time Torkoal switched in, leaving Sandstorm as the dominant weather. Venusaur — paralyzed and resisted by Gholdengo's Good as Gold — could not threaten anyone with Sludge Bomb or charge Solar Beam reliably. Torkoal died on Turn 5 to Gholdengo's Shadow Ball, ending any remaining weather control. Skarmory entered too late (Turn 5) with the game already decided and was whittled down by Tauros-Paldea-Aqua's Close Combat and Gholdengo's Shadow Ball. Aegislash and Heracross were left on the bench despite both being strong matchup answers: Aegislash threatens Gholdengo and Grimmsnarl, and Heracross's Fighting STAB threatens Tyranitar and Tauros. The team preview plan (sun offense with Charizard-Mega/Torkoal/Venusaur) was predictable and directly countered by the opponent's Sand Stream + Gholdengo + Grimmsnarl screens core. Between-game adjustments from Game 1 to Game 2 did not meaningfully alter the gameplan or team selection, so they did not help.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a rematch: (1) Drop Charizard — it is Mega Stone-dependent, fodder to Fake Out + Rock Slide, and the sun plan is countered by their Sand core. (2) Bring Aegislash and Heracross; Aegislash pressures Gholdengo and Grimmsnarl, Heracross threatens Tyranitar and Tauros with Fighting STAB. (3) Abandon the sun weather war — Torkoal's Drought cannot coexist with Sand Stream, so either pivot Torkoal to a non-weather-support role or replace it entirely. (4) Prepare for dual screens + Sand: bring a rapid spinner or Defog user (Torkoal's Rapid Spin is useful but it must survive to use it), and pack Steel- or Poison-type coverage to hit Gholdengo. (5) Expect Fake Out flinch pressure on lead and have a non-Fake-Out-vulnerable lead or a safe switch ready. (6) Note that Gholdengo is fully immune to status via Good as Gold — do not rely on Sleep Powder or Toxic.
reflections.notebook: CONFIRMED OPPONENT TENDENCIES (rematch notes): Sand Stream core confirmed — Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Adamant, Rock Slide/EQ/Protect/Thunder Wave), Excadrill (Life Orb, Sand Rush, not yet revealed in-game but on roster). Gholdengo is the 4th slot: Leftovers, Modest, Good as Gold grants full status immunity; runs Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Recover, Protect; walls Venusaur's STAB entirely and recovers freely. Grimmsnarl is the Light Clay dual-screens setter (Prankster Reflect + Light Screen + Fake Out + Spirit Break); screens last 5 turns with Light Clay, enabling Gholdengo and Tauros to overwhelm. Tauros-Paldea-Aqua: Aqua form, Adamant, Intimidate, Sitrus Berry; moves Close Combat / WaveCrash / AquaJet / Protect; physical wallbreaker that tanks hits and punishes with Intimidate drops. Opponent has a clear Sand + Screens + Recover stall-break strategy. STRATEGIC FACTS: Fake Out + flinch on Turn 1 is their standard opener to gut sun leads. Gholdengo laughs at Sludge Bomb and Sleep Powder. Sandstorm + Spikes + Close Combat is the kill condition against physical walls. CharizarditeY is expended — Mega Charizard Y is unavailable for future games this season. PREP CONCLUSIONS: Sun offense is a losing matchup here; pivot to a different win condition. Prioritize Aegislash + Heracross in the 4-slot game selection. Bring a Defog/Rapid Spin answer to clear Spikes if Torkoal is kept. Pack Steel/Poison coverage for Gholdengo. Do not rely on status moves against Good as Gold.
